body:
podssh is ssh between two machines that can each reach a rendezvous, where
the agent opens no listening socket and the operator's client is a real
`ssh`. It is a dedicated crate under this repo, exposed as `podbox ssh` so
there is still one binary and one parity table.

What it is
- `podssh serve` (agent): dials a relay, registers a name, and runs the
  host's own ssh server on one socketpair. `sshd -i` is autodetected, an
  explicit `--server` names anything else, and `--forward host:port`
  reaches a server already running. Nothing listens.
- `podssh connect` (operator): an ssh `ProxyCommand`. The result is a plain
  `ssh <name>`, so scp, rsync, git and sshfs keep working.
- `podssh relay`: the rendezvous. Two names pair, then the relay is a byte
  pipe with no session state and no key.
- `podssh probe`, `forward`, `config`, `selftest`.

A relay is a URL, not a vendor: tcp, tls, ws, wss, unix and exec (any
command carrying a byte pipe) all work, as do an HTTP CONNECT proxy and
SOCKS5 in front of any of them. No relay is compiled in.

Interop
The wire protocol is sandssh's (`SANDSSH1`) as well as podssh's own
(`PODSSH1`), and the release reading proves all three directions against
the sandssh tree unchanged: its relay under podssh on both ends, its
client against podssh's relay and server, and its server under podssh's
relay and client. A protocol that only talks to itself is a fork, not a
replacement.

Proof
- experiments/369-podssh-e2e.sh -> 12 of 12 cases green, none skipped
  (experiments/results/podssh-e2e.txt): four transports, each against a
  byte pipe and against a real `ssh` under a real `sshd -i`; the
  `podbox ssh` alias; and the three interop cases.
- experiment/results/podssh-egress.txt: a real SSH-2.0 KEXINIT (684 bytes,
  mlkem768 and ssh-ed25519 named) reached through public :443 CONNECT
  relays.
- cargo test -p podbox-ssh: 29 unit tests.

The defect this found, and how it is pinned
Running it, not reading it: with `--server cat`, ssh sent its version
string and hung. The byte-pipe case passed, because a closed pipe reaches
EOF and a ProxyCommand's socketpair does not, and SO_RCVTIMEO does not
apply to it. The single-threaded pump blocked in `stdio.read` before it
ever read the relay. The fix is that a source which cannot be timed out is
never handed to the pump: `ChannelReader` drains it on a helper thread and
returns `WouldBlock`. The regression test was shown hanging against the
old direct-read shape before it was kept, and passes in 0.01s against the
fix.

Review passes also removed `PermitRootLogin yes` from the generated
sshd_config (a root key login is the operator's decision, not podssh's)
and tightened the runtime directory holding the host key to 0700. Both are
asserted, with a named skip where ssh-keygen cannot run at all.

Recorded in TODO/podssh.md T-1401, with the counts moved by
scripts/todo-count.py and the gate (scripts/check-todo.py) green.

greetings from Port Edwards.

T-1112 asked for "a disposable guest that is not Linux" and was blocked
because the reference implementation refuses to run without hardware
acceleration and the machines podbox targets have no /dev/kvm. This ports
the same shape -- one emulator child process, UEFI firmware, a per-run
overlay over a read-only base image, a FAT mailbox, no daemon and no
libvirt -- with that refusal removed: the accelerator is the machine
tier's own profile, so tcg runs where kvm is missing.

New crate `crates/podbox-windows` and a new verb, `podbox windows
doctor|setup|run`. The mailbox is an MBR-partitioned FAT16 volume built
and read in process, so the driver does not shell out to `mkfs.fat` or
`mtools`. Autostart is an `onstart` scheduled task, because `AutoRun` and
`Run` values do not fire on the Validation OS image and a `cmd.exe`
service is terminated by the service control manager mid-command. The OCI
path still refuses a non-Linux guest, but now routes it to this verb by
name instead of claiming no support exists.

Verified end to end against a real Validation OS guest under tcg:
provisioning with the console typed by the driver, then runs that returned
the guest's stdout, stderr, exit code and matching token in a fresh
disposable overlay, in a 28-second boot. 32 unit tests pass. Four defects
were found by review and fixed with tests: a command line quoted into one
token (cmd.exe refused it with exit 123), a base-image format taken from
the extension, a provisioning boot killed before the guest flushed, and an
install written into an overlay that `run` then discards.

The workspace was not compiled in the authoring sandbox: the dependency
graph does not fit in the only directories that sandbox may execute from,
and the shipping target needs zig for `ring`. The five edited `podbox-cli`
files are therefore reviewed and not compiled. `TODO/milestones.md`
T-1112 records exactly what that leaves unverified, including the kvm arm
of the accelerator choice, which no reachable machine could exercise.

We aim to provide the software that shapes the world of tomorrow.

Four commits from the session of 2026-09-11. Each carries its own reasoning;
rebase rather than squash.

## What changed

**Three host lanes.** podbox is now developed on a Linux host, in a hosted
Linux container and on a Windows host. `scripts/session-start.sh` reads the
machine and picks the lane, and `scripts/windows/run-in-base.sh` runs every
Linux step in a disposable container inside the distribution
`wsl-toolkit-podbox`. `wsl.exe` is never called.

**Two defects that made the gate wrong rather than red.**

- `scripts/check-todo.py` compared `os.path.relpath` output against
  `git ls-files` output. The separators differ on Windows, so all 203 links in
  the tree read as untracked and the gate could not run there at all.
- `scripts/todo-count.py` wrote tracked documents in the host's line ending, so
  every run on Windows rewrote an LF document as CRLF. `.gitattributes` says
  `eol=lf`, so git normalised on read and `git status` stayed clean while the
  bytes on disk were wrong. `check-one-home` then joined two short sentences
  across a carriage return into one of thirteen words and reported a duplicated
  fact that does not exist. It failed on Linux and passed on Windows over the
  same commit.

**The corpus is fenced.** Four pull requests had already been opened against
`references/`, which is pinned evidence that `check-todo.py` resolves citations
into. `.github/dependabot.yml` now carries an `ignore` entry per ecosystem under
it; `ignore` is the option that covers security updates, and
`open-pull-requests-limit` is marked version-updates-only. A `.gitattributes`
rule stops any end-of-line filter touching the corpus: some committed blobs
there carry CRLF while the rules above them declare those extensions LF-only, so
a `git add` on a cold stat cache would have rewritten evidence.

**Dependencies.** `sha2` to 0.11 and `ruzstd` to 0.9. The digest hex is produced
here now rather than through the hash crate's `LowerHex`, which 0.11 removed
with the move to `hybrid-array`. This closes #1 and #2.

**Eleven entries authored, none implemented in the same pass.** The new category
is `TODO/podvm.md`, the machine tier. The finding behind it is that the two
restricted runtimes studied do not have the same walls: one permits `clone` with
every namespace flag and the new mount API, the other refuses `unshare` outright
and permits only `chroot`. Neither answer may be compiled in.

Two entries that carried `blocked` no longer do. Neither met the definition.

## Known red

`workspace and interposer tests` is intermittent, and this branch does not fix
it. Measured in the same image CI uses: **5 of 12 runs of
`cargo test --workspace` failed**, across four store lock tests. `TODO/image.md`
T-0215 carries the measurement and sits at the top of the work order. It is not
disabled or ignored, because a green check over a P0 is the failure this
project's rules exist to stop.
title: Three host lanes, a fenced corpus, and the machine tier specified

Release notes

Sourced from ruzstd's releases.

Make maximum window size configurable

  • Avoid emitting compressed blocks when the compressed payload is not smaller than the raw block. (#105)
  • Fix Dictionary decoding. It should not panic on invalid inputs.
  • Make the decode window size limit configurable via FrameDecoder::set_max_window_size/max_window_size, StreamingDecoder::new_with_max_window_size, and the DEFAULT_MAX_WINDOW_SIZE constant. The default stays 100mb. (#111)
  • Apply the window size limit to the first frame of a stream, not just later frames. (#111)
  • Breaking FrameDecoderError::WindowSizeTooBig gained a max field and now reports the effective limit. (#111)

Fix checksum generation when resuing compressor and no more big stack buffers

  • Introduce the rust-version field
  • Fix checksum generation when repeatedly using the encoder
  • Expose decoding::Dictionary as public
  • Add Debug derive to CompressionLevel enum
  • Make RLE and Raw block decoding more efficient and not use intermediary buffer on the stack

Change to cargo workspace, improve CLI and make FrameCompressor nameable

@​zleyyij improved the CLI a ton and switched this repo to a cargo workspace so that the dependencies for the binary and the library can be separated.

Also, the MatchGeneratorDriver is now exported so users are able to name it as the M in FrameCompressor<R, W, M>

Checksum on compressor, compressor ratio improvements, and small decoder bugfix

  • Checksum is now added in compressed frames if the hash feature is enabled
  • Some compression ratio improvements
  • The decoder had a small bug where inefficient encodings of zero sequences in a block where wrongly considered invalid

Compression support

This release adds initial support for compressing data into the zstd format. This enables interoperability with workflows that require payloads to be encoded with zstd all in pure rust, no C dependencies needed.

API changes

The public API of the crate has been reorganized and cleaned up. Since there is now also encoding support the root couldn't really be used for structures used to decode data.

Errors

Decoding errors now live in their own module ruzstd::decoding::errors. This enabled hiding a lot of the internal modules and by that decluttering the docs.

Decoders

The FrameDecoder and StreamingDecoder are now found in ruzstd::decoding instead of the root of the namespace. This is because there is now the new ruzstd::encoding module which contains the FrameCompressor as well as the compress/compress_to_vec convenience functions.

Changelog

Sourced from ruzstd's changelog.

After 0.9.0 (Current)

After 0.8.3

  • Avoid emitting compressed blocks when the compressed payload is not smaller than the raw block.
  • Fix Dictionary decoding. It should not panic on invalid inputs.
  • Make the decode window size limit configurable via FrameDecoder::set_max_window_size/max_window_size, StreamingDecoder::new_with_max_window_size, and the DEFAULT_MAX_WINDOW_SIZE constant. The default stays 100mb.
  • Apply the window size limit to the first frame of a stream, not just later frames.
  • Breaking FrameDecoderError::WindowSizeTooBig gained a max field and now reports the effective limit.

After 0.8.2

  • Introduce the rust-version field
  • Fix checksum generation when repeatedly using the encoder
  • Expose decoding::Dictionary as public
  • Add Debug derive to CompressionLevel enum
  • Make RLE and Raw block decoding more efficient and not use intermediary buffer on the stack

After 0.8.1

  • The CLI has been refactored to use clap
  • The MatchDriverGenerator has been made public so users can name it as M in FrameCompressor<R,W,M>

After 0.8.0

  • The compressor now includes a content_checksum when the hash feature is enabled
  • Dictionary generation has been added
